recall.minute: A DFNN stacks layers that compute $\mathbf z=\mathbf h\mathbf W+\mathbf b$ then $\mathbf h=\sigma(\mathbf z)$. Non-linear activations are what make depth useful; without them the network is one linear map, which cannot solve XOR. Training picks a loss matched to the output (MSE/identity, BCE/sigmoid, CCE/softmax) so the output error is $\hat{\mathbf y}-\mathbf y$. Backprop pushes that error back with $\boldsymbol\delta^{(\ell)}=(\boldsymbol\delta^{(\ell+1)}\mathbf W^\top)\odot\sigma'$, giving $\partial J/\partial\mathbf W=\frac1B\mathbf H^\top\boldsymbol\delta$, and mini-batch SGD updates every weight. Depth builds hierarchies efficiently but brings vanishing/exploding gradients; ReLU, He/Xavier init, normalisation and residual connections handle them.
